thread:
Alice Chen: paging: alert flood from euw2-monitoring - multiple HTTP health checks for model-serving pool 'euw2-ml-prod' are returning 502/timeout. seeing ~15% error rate on frontend routes, apiserver 503s for some customers. pinging SRE.

oncall-bot: Incident detected: euw2-region-healthchecks - threshold breached (15m) -> paging eng-oncall. Incident ID: INC-2025-0421-euw2.

Mateo Rivera: I'm looking. can someone drop the last 20s of probe logs? `kubectl logs -n monitoring probe-euw2 --tail=200` would help.

Priya Kaur: pulling probe logs now, tail looks like repeated connection resets to 10.8.0.2:9200 and `socket timeout` against probe endpoint. also see a bunch of `ENETUNREACH` in the traceroute.

Samir (neteng): Hitting this from net layer: we've got a short control-plane routing flap in AZ-B (euw2-azb). BGP withdrawal observed for a set of prefixes toward our NAT gateway cluster. Cloud provider ticket opened (SR# 3458123).

Mateo Rivera: thanks @Samir. can you confirm if this is affecting only probe subnet or also customer traffic? early customer reports indicate intermittent 503s.

Samir (neteng): Initial telemetry: probe VMs and a subset of node egress paths are hit. Data plane to certain external health targets (route53 healthcheck IPs) is being rerouted -> increased latency and some connection resets. suggests route churn rather than complete outage.

Jenna (cust-succ): I've started triaging customer reports - three paying accounts reported API timeouts within the last 10m. Notified them we're investigating and will update in 15.

Mateo Rivera: mitigation options: (1) temporary disable external health checks for the cluster to stop noisy pages, (2) route probe traffic to alternate targets, (3) failover traffic to other regions (expensive). Prefer (1)+(2) to gain breathing room. thoughts?

Priya Kaur: I can push a quick override to monitoring to silence the alarms for 30m (`/monitoring/silence INC-2025-0421-euw2 30m`) while we investigate. keeping automated page suppression on so we don't get pager storm.

Mateo Rivera: do it. also create a canary check that hits an internal endpoint instead of external health targets. add config here: ```yaml
# quick canary check
- name: euw2-internal-canary
  type: http
  target: http://10.8.1.10:8080/health
  interval: 10s
```

Priya Kaur: silence applied. creating canary. pushing check now.

oncall-bot: Monitoring silence applied by Priya Kaur for 30m on euw2-region-healthchecks.

Mateo Rivera: good. Samir, any ETA from provider on BGP/routing fix?

Samir (neteng): Cloud tier1 says they've identified a flap with a regional router and are deploying a fix; estimated 12-18 minutes. I'll post updates.

Alice Chen: customer impact note: affected accounts saw elevated 5xxs during 17:39-17:52 UTC, some retry loops gave latency spikes. we should collect example request IDs for postmortem. Jenna, can you gather the request IDs you saw?

Jenna (cust-succ): yes collecting now, will DM a list. also prepped a short status msg for impacted customers: "We are investigating intermittent API errors in EU-West-2; no data loss expected. Engineers are working on mitigation." want me to send?

Mateo Rivera: hold on external comms until we confirm failover/silence. use language "intermittent" and commit to next update in 30m.

Priya Kaur: cloud provider just pushed a partial fix; BGP announcements stabilizing on their side, I see fewer ENETUNREACH in logs. metrics glance: probe failures dropping from 15% -> 3% over last 2 mins.

Samir (neteng): confirming - routing converged on most prefixes. a small subset of NAT instances still showing elevated retransmits, will keep monitoring.

Mateo Rivera: re-enable monitoring alerts but keep a higher threshold for 10m window to avoid immediate re-page. I'll open an incident ticket and hand-off to ENG-SRE for postmortem. creating ticket INC-2025-0421-euw2-detailed.

oncall-bot: PagerDuty: incident INC-2025-0421-euw2 created by Mateo Rivera. Assigned: eng-sre. Handoff scheduled at 18:15 UTC.

Alice Chen: summary for handoff: short-lived routing flap in euw2-azb led to probe telemetry suppression and transient 5xxs for some customer requests. mitigation: monitoring silence + internal canary + cloud fix. impact window ~ 17:39-17:52 UTC, ~15% peak error rate, now resolved to <1%.

Jenna (cust-succ): sent customer notice to affected orgs at 17:58 UTC with a follow-up promise for postmortem.

Mateo Rivera: next actions: 1) ENG-SRE to gather packet captures/flow logs for 17:30-18:00 2) NetEng to pull provider route history and SR updates 3) Monitoring to validate probe config and consider moving healthcheck targets inside region. I'll update incident ticket with these tasks.

Samir (neteng): will attach BGP update history and cloud SR timeline to the ticket.

Priya Kaur: removing the temporary canary after 10m, monitoring back to normal thresholds. leaving silence until incident Handoff if no regression.

Alice Chen: handing off to @eng-sre for formal postmortem. thanks all for quick responses. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2025-0421-euw2 status: mitigated. Handoff to eng-sre at 18:15 UTC.

Mateo Rivera: logging final note: please include example request IDs, probe logs, and cloud SR in postmortem. closing thread from on-call perspective, will keep ticket open for postmortem artifacts.

Jenna (cust-succ): will follow up with customers when postmortem is ready.

Samir (neteng): provider confirmed root cause: partial control-plane routing instability during a maintenance window they didn't flag correctly. they marked SR resolved at 18:10 UTC. attaching SR note to ticket.

Alice Chen: thanks team.
